target_year_over_year_context.explanation:
Both disclosures describe the NVIDIA RTX gaming platform features, specifically ray tracing for realistic rendering and DLSS (Deep Learning Super Sampling) AI technology for boosting frame rates. See original sentences nvda_2024_1_P026_S002, nvda_2024_1_P026_S003, nvda_2024_1_P026_S005 and nvda_2025_1_P026_S002, nvda_2025_1_P026_S003, nvda_2025_1_P026_S005.

Both disclosures identify RTX as the 'AI PC leader' leveraging a specific installed base metric. The 2024 disclosure cites 'over 100 million AI capable PCs' and '500+ applications', while the 2025 disclosure (D025) cites the same 'over 100 million AI capable PCs' installed base but updates the application count to 'more than 700'. This confirms they refer to the same specific topic (RTX AI PC leadership status) despite the update in volume metrics.

comparisons.peer_summary: AMD offers mobile Ryzen processors with leadership performance and battery life, including the 2024 release of Ryzen AI 300 Series with NPUs and Zen 5 architecture, previous generations with Zen 4/Zen 3+/Zen 2, and Ryzen Z1 Series for handheld gaming.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVDA and AMD disclose their positioning in the AI PC market through specific processor architectures and installed bases. NVDA claims leadership via its RTX GPU ecosystem and an installed base of over 100 million AI-capable PCs, driven by software acceleration (e.g., DLSS) and a robust developer suite. AMD similarly targets the AI PC market by releasing the Ryzen AI 300 Series with NPUs and Zen 5 architecture in 2024, alongside previous generations with NPUs (Zen 4). While NVDA focuses on the GPU-centric 'AI PC' software ecosystem and installed base size, AMD focuses on the CPU/NPU-centric hardware specifications (Zen 5 architecture, NPU integration) for local AI performance.

sentences.text: RTX GPUs will also accelerate a new generation of AI applications.
With an installed base of over 100 million AI capable PCs, more than 500 RTX AI-enabled applications and games, and a robust suite of development tools, RTX is already the AI PC leader.
We released AMD Ryzen AI 300 Series processors featuring a NPU for next-generation AI PCs featuring our latest "Zen 5" architecture in 2024.
Our AMD Ryzen mobile processors offer a leadership combination of performance, battery life, and immersive visual experiences for PCs.
